reasoning: Both models that successfully completed analysis (qwen3-235b and deepseek-v4-flash) found the PKGBUILD safe. The package downloads a prebuilt binary from the project's own GitHub releases with a pinned SHA-256 checksum, performs standard modifications (WebKit workaround wrapper script, asset path patching for Tauri), and contains no obfuscated code, execution of untrusted content, or data exfiltration. The 'inconclusive' results were caused entirely by tool errors (HTTP 400 API failure, parsing failure), not security concerns. The openrouter report is advisory-only and from an older pkgver (1.0.7), so it carries no weight.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool failures, not substantive security analysis differences. Qwen3-235b failed on .SRCINFO with HTTP 400; openrouter/free failed to parse its own response. Deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed both files and found them safe. The two successful PKGBUILD analyses agreed on all security-relevant points: pinned checksum, legitimate upstream source, standard packaging modifications.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b: .SRCINFO review failed with HTTP 400 BadRequestError
openrouter/free: PKGBUILD review failed with parsing error, only 1 of 2 files reviewed
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, parsing errors) should be distinguished from security inconclusiveness - a failed API call is not evidence of risk
Advisory reports from older package versions should be clearly deprioritized or excluded from verdict calculation
When multiple models agree on safety with consistent reasoning about pinned checksums and standard modifications, tool errors in other reports should not override the consensus
